name: Functional Variant of Guillain-Barré Syndrome

criteria.description: Acute onset of symmetrical limb weakness progressing over days to weeks
Absence of demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies despite clinical presentation
Normal cerebrospinal fluid protein levels without albuminocytologic dissociation
Presence of functional neurological signs inconsistent with typical GBS

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Acute symmetrical limb weakness with absence of demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies plus either normal CSF protein or presence of functional neurological signs
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of classic Guillain-Barré syndrome and other neuropathies.

searchTerms: weakness in hands and feet symmetrically
distal limb muscle weakness both sides
equal weakness in distal arms and legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Flaccid paralysis without objective sensory loss
searchTerms: loss of muscle strength without sensory loss

common.symptomName: Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes
searchTerms: loss of knee or ankle reflexes

common.symptomName: Functional neurological signs inconsistent with organic neuropathy
searchTerms: neurological signs not matching nerve damage
extreme tiredness not explained by nerve problems
fatigue worse than expected from neurological signs

occasional.symptomName: Transient paresthesias without objective sensory deficit
Mild autonomic symptoms such as orthostatic dizziness
searchTerms: mild autonomic symptoms like dizziness on standing
lightheadedness due to blood pressure drop
orthostatic dizziness and mild autonomic issues
muscle tone changes varying over time

rare.symptomName: Autonomic instability with blood pressure fluctuations
searchTerms: autonomic nervous system causing BP swings
blood pressure instability from autonomic dysfunction

laboratory: Normal cerebrospinal fluid protein without albuminocytologic dissociation
imaging: Normal brain and spinal MRI excluding alternative diagnoses
other: Nerve conduction studies showing absence of demyelination or axonal loss
Presence of functional neurological signs on clinical examination

distinguishingFeatures: Elevated CSF protein with albuminocytologic dissociation
Demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies
Psychogenic symptoms without objective neurological deficits

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness with respiratory compromise
Presence of objective sensory loss or demyelination on nerve conduction studies
Signs of autonomic instability such as severe blood pressure fluctuations
